recreation_brief: 1. Set the slide background to light gray #E8E8E8 with a hairline border. 2. Place a centered text box in the header (top 0-10%) with red #E74C3C text reading "Model Kernelization". 3. Place a gray #95A5A6 circle badge in the top-right header containing dark slate #2C3E50 text "20". 4. In the top flow left column (left 0-35%), place two dark slate #2C3E50 rectangular vector boxes labeled "a1, b1" and "a2, b2". 5. Draw a red #E74C3C right-pointing arrow from the top-left vector boxes to the top-right pane. 6. Place a light blue #D6EAF8 rectangular pane in the top-right with a red #E74C3C header reading "Normal Model". 7. Inside the Normal Model pane, add dark slate #2C3E50 text "Calculate a^T b" and the label "O/P". 8. Place a blue #3498DB horizontal guidance pill across the middle (vertical 40-50%) with white text "Map Input data to higher dimensions Before Apply to the model". 9. In the bottom flow left column (left 0-35%), place two dark slate #2C3E50 rectangular vector boxes labeled "a1, b1" and "a2, b2". 10. Draw a red #E74C3C right-pointing arrow from the bottom-left vector boxes to the bottom-center box. 11. Place a white rectangular box with a red #E74C3C border in the bottom-center containing dark slate #2C3E50 text "Vectors Mapping" and the equation "a, b -> u, v". 12. To the right of the Vectors Mapping box, place two purple #8E44AD rectangular vector boxes labeled "u1, v1" and "u2, v2". 13. Place a light green #D5F5E3 rectangular pane in the bottom-right with a red #E74C3C header reading "Kernelized Model". 14. Inside the Kernelized Model pane, add dark slate #2C3E50 text "Calculate u^T v" and the label "O/R". 15. Add a small gray #7F8C8D cursor arrow icon immediately to the right of the "O/R" label inside the Kernelized Model pane. 16. Add purple #8E44AD text "Higher Computational Complexity" inside the Kernelized Model pane below the calculation. 17. Place a purple #8E44AD chip in the bottom-left corner (left 0-20%, vertical 85-95%) with text "Higher Computational Complexity". 18. Render the equations "a^T b", "u^T v", and "a, b -> u, v" in a standard mathematical typeface.
